en: I am not good enough to be truly loved.
Other people are more valuable, more interesting and better than me.
I always lack something to be enough.
I do not deserve a good life, love and happiness.
My worth depends on what others think of me.
I have to please others to be accepted and loved.
If someone criticizes me, it means something is wrong with me.
I need others' attention and admiration to feel worthy.
If people get to know the real me, they will not accept me.
I have to hide my flaws so I do not lose others' respect.
I must not make mistakes, or I will lose my worth.
I have to appear stronger, more confident or more successful than I really feel.
My worth depends on what I have achieved.
I have to constantly prove that I am worth something.
I am allowed to be satisfied with myself only when I have achieved more.
If I am not useful to others, I do not feel needed or significant.
I have to adapt to others so I do not lose their acceptance.
I do not know who I am if I am not looking at myself through others' judgment.
My true wishes and needs are not as important as other people's wishes.
I cannot be fully myself and at the same time be accepted and loved.
I am afraid that the person I love will leave me sooner or later.
I have to try harder than the other person for them to stay with me.
If my partner becomes colder or pulls away, I immediately think I no longer matter to them.
I find it hard to feel safe in a relationship, even when my partner assures me of their love.
I cannot fully trust my partner, because they could betray or deceive me.
I have to know where my partner is, who they are with and what they are doing.
If my partner pays attention to others, I feel threatened and less valuable.
I have to monitor the relationship to keep it from falling apart.
If I let someone get too close, they could hurt me.
It is easier for me to pull away than to openly show what I really feel.
When a relationship gets too close, I feel the urge to run away or shut down.
I cannot fully relax and be myself even with the person I love.
I have to give up my needs to keep the relationship.
If I say what I really want, my partner might reject me.
I feel responsible for my partner's emotions and well-being.
I find it hard to say what I want and to ask for what matters to me in a relationship.
I have to provoke my partner's reaction to be sure they care.
I pull away, go silent or withhold closeness when I feel hurt or misunderstood.
I repeat relationship patterns that hurt me, even though I know their consequences.
I do not believe I can experience love without struggle, tension and emotional pain.
In childhood my emotions and needs were not important enough.
My needs are a burden to other people.
I have to cope on my own, because others cannot be relied on.
No one really understands me, so I have to stay alone with my feelings.
I am never good enough in my parents' eyes.
Mistakes mean that I am bad and incompetent.
I have to hide my true opinion to avoid criticism.
I am responsible for making my parents proud of me.
I am loved only when I behave correctly.
I have to fulfill others' expectations so I do not lose their love.
If I am different from my family, I am betraying them.
To be accepted, I have to hide what I really want.
Since childhood I had to take care of everyone else.
I am responsible for my parents' emotions and their happiness.
I have to be strong, because there is no room for my weakness in the family.
I am allowed to feel good only when everyone around me is okay.
If I choose myself, I am selfish and a bad family member.
I owe my parents for everything they gave me.
I have to stay silent about family problems so I do not break the family apart.
I cannot live differently, because I have to stay loyal to my family's fate.
Something bad could happen to me at any moment.
The world is a dangerous place, and I cannot protect myself.
I can never fully relax, because something could happen.
If I am not vigilant, I will miss the danger.
I have to control everything to feel safe.
If I do not know what will happen, I cannot feel calm.
I myself have to foresee and prevent every possible problem.
If something does not go according to my plan, I lose my sense of safety.
I cannot trust people, because they will betray me.
Relying on others is dangerous.
If I show vulnerability, someone will use it against me.
I always have to rely only on myself.
If I lose what I have, I will not be able to survive it.
Making mistakes is dangerous, because the consequences could ruin everything.
If I lose control of a situation, everything will fall apart.
I have to avoid risks so I never get hurt.
I cannot influence what happens to me.
I have no one to protect me, so I am alone.
I cannot cope with strong emotions and fears.
Only when I am fully prepared am I allowed to act.
My emotions are a nuisance, and I have to suppress them.
I have no right to feel bad when others have it harder.
I have to be strong and pretend that everything is fine.
If I start feeling my emotions, I will lose control.
Crying and showing feelings means being weak.
I am ashamed of what I really feel.
If I show that I am hurt, others will use my weakness.
My anger makes me a bad person.
I feel good only when others are satisfied with me.
If someone is dissatisfied with me, I feel guilty.
I need others' attention to feel emotionally fulfilled.
If someone does not understand me, I feel rejected and worthless.
It is easier to feel nothing than to experience pain.
I have to distract myself so I do not have to be alone with myself.
If I open up my feelings, I will become dependent on the other person.
I have to keep people at a distance so no one hurts me.
I am guilty of feeling bad and not being able to pull myself together.
I have to be happy and positive so others do not have a hard time.
I must not be angry at people I love.
I do not deserve peace until I have solved all my problems.
My worth depends on how successful I am at work.
I have to constantly prove that I am capable enough.
If I am not better than others, I am not good enough.
If I do not achieve what I set out to, I am a failure.
I have to do everything perfectly to be appreciated.
I must not make mistakes, because others will lose respect for me.
Until I am fully ready, I should not start.
If my work is not flawless, it is better not to show it to anyone.
If I become visible, others will criticize or judge me.
I have no right to ask for higher pay for my work.
If I talk about my achievements, others will think I am arrogant.
I have to wait until someone notices my potential.
I am not capable enough to carry out my plans.
My ideas are not good enough to be realized.
If I start and fail, I will have embarrassed myself.
I have to wait for the right moment to start.
I always have to work more to deserve rest.
If I do not do everything myself, nothing will be done right.
I have to be productive all the time, otherwise I am wasting time.
If I stop working, I will lose my significance and identity.
I will never have enough money to feel secure.
There will always be too little money to live the way I want.
If I spend money, I will run out of it later.
I have to save as much as possible, because scarcity may come.
It is hard for me to earn, because I am not valuable enough.
I do not deserve to live in wealth and prosperity.
I have to work very hard to deserve money.
I feel uncomfortable asking for payment for my work.
If I have more money than my family, I am betraying them.
Money makes people selfish and bad.
I have to help others financially, even if I do not have enough myself.
I have no right to live better while my relatives are struggling.
Any financial risk could lead me to catastrophe.
I do not know how to handle money, so it is better not to change anything.
If I lose money, it will prove that I am a failure.
I have to be completely certain before making a financial decision.
I feel uncomfortable accepting gifts, help or financial support.
I must not spend on myself until everything else is taken care of.
If I have money, I have to spend it quickly.
Big money and prosperity are not meant for people like me.
My life has no real meaning or significance.
I do not know what I really want from my life.
My life is not going the way it should.
I have not found my true place in the world.
Change is dangerous, and it is better to stay with the familiar.
If I leave my habitual life, I will lose everything.
I will not be able to cope with the future.
Better to change nothing than to risk making a mistake.
I am afraid of making the wrong decision and ruining my life.
Someone else has to tell me what I should do.
I am responsible for making sure all my decisions are right.
If I choose myself, I will let down or hurt others.
I have made too many mistakes to start over.
I cannot forgive myself for the past.
I have missed my chance to live the way I wanted.
The past has determined my future.
I will start living when everything is sorted out.
I first have to fulfill my duties, only then may I think about myself.
It is too late to start something new.
I always have to want more, not be content.
I have no right to refuse other people.
If I set boundaries, people will stop loving me.
I have to adapt to others to avoid conflict.
Other people's needs are always more important than mine.
If someone is angry with me, I have done something wrong.
I have to avoid conflict at all costs.
If I stand up for myself, I will be selfish or aggressive.
I have to make sure everyone is satisfied with me.
Other people decide how I should live.
I do not have the power to change what dissatisfies me.
I have to control everything so others do not take advantage of me.
If I do not take charge, others will make decisions for me.
I am responsible for making sure everything is fine for others.
If something goes wrong, it is my fault.
I have to do everything that is expected of me.
I must not disappoint others, even if it harms me.
I have no right to demand to be treated with respect.
I cannot rely on my own judgment and decisions.
I have to wait for others' permission to do what I want.
I am powerless when someone does not approve of my choices.
My body has no right to safety and respect.
I have to stay silent about what I went through to avoid consequences.
I myself am to blame for being treated violently.
I always have to be ready to defend myself, because the danger may repeat.
I have no right to decide what happens to my body.
I have to accept the other person's wishes so they do not reject me.
After what happened I am damaged and less valuable.
I have no right to talk about what happened to me.
I will never be able to feel safe again.
I have to live in constant readiness, because everything could collapse.
If I survived while others died, I have no right to feel good.
I will not be able to regain control over my life after what I went through.
I will never be able to get over this loss.
My life will never be meaningful again.
I have to hide my pain so I do not become a burden to others.
I do not deserve help until I cope on my own.
My pain will never ease.
I am a burden to other people.
I have no right to ask for help, because others have it harder.
My life is not valuable enough to fight for.
